{{Short description|German-American mathematician (1911–1973)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2021}}
'''Otto Franz Georg Schilling''' (3 November 1911 – 20 June 1973) was a German-American mathematician known as one of the leading [[algebra]]ists of his time.<ref>{{citation|title=Modern Algebra and the Rise of Mathematical Structures|first=Leo|last=Corry|publisher=Springer|year=2004|isbn=9783764370022|page=222|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WdGbeyehoCoC&pg=PA222}}.</ref>

He was born in [[Apolda]] and studied in the 1930s at the [[Universität Jena]] and the [[Universität Göttingen]] under [[Emmy Noether]]. After Noether was forced to leave Germany by the Nazis, he found a new advisor in [[Helmut Hasse]],<ref name="a3">{{citation|title=A3 & His Algebra: How a Boy from Chicago's West Side Became a Force in American Mathematics|first=Nancy|last=Albert-Goldberg|publisher=iUniverse|year=2005|isbn=9780595328178|page=122|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Id-v3q__QfoC&pg=PA122}}.</ref> and obtained his Ph.D. from [[Marburg University]] in 1934 on the thesis ''Über gewisse Beziehungen zwischen der Arithmetik hyperkomplexer Zahlsysteme und algebraischer Zahlkörper''.<ref name="mg"/> He then was [[post doc]] at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] before moving to [[Institute for Advanced Study]] 1935–37<ref>{{cite web|title=Otto Franz Georg Schilling|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/otto-franz-georg-schilling}}</ref> and the [[Johns Hopkins University]] 1937–39. He became an instructor with the [[University of Chicago]] in 1939,<ref name="a3"/> promoted to assistant professor 1943, associate 1945 and full professor in 1958. In 1961 he moved to [[Purdue University]]. He died in [[Highland Park, Illinois]]. His students were, among others, the game theorist [[Anatol Rapoport]] and the mathematician [[Harley Flanders]].<ref name="mg">{{Mathgenealogy|id=6367}}</ref>
